title: Recoverable Depreciation Hold on the Reconstruction Final Draw
content:
The depreciation hold on the final draw of a Reconstruction contract keeps out the recoverable depreciation the carrier has not paid, which it releases only once the work is shown complete by the final invoice and the completion date. It reads the claim file kept under Insurance Claim Services: the dwelling depreciation withheld on its scope approvals, the dwelling depreciation the carrier has released, the amounts written off as depreciation forfeited, and whether its claim arrangement bills carrier-denied amounts to the customer.

**Carrier-funded.** A final draw is carrier-funded when its funding route, set by the base draw rule from the linked claim file, is not the customer: the claim file has a dwelling payment the carrier issued to the company directly (contractor direct), by a check naming the insured and the company (insured two-party), or into the mortgagee's loss-draft account (mortgagee loss draft). On any other final draw the customer funds the draw.

**Rule.** On a carrier-funded final draw:

- when the claim arrangement bills carrier-denied amounts to the customer, the hold is the dwelling depreciation withheld on the claim file's approvals less the dwelling depreciation the carrier has released, never below zero, the part written off as depreciation forfeited being the customer's;
- when the claim arrangement does not bill carrier-denied amounts to the customer, the hold is that withheld depreciation less the depreciation released and less the amounts written off as depreciation forfeited, never below zero.

On a final draw that is not carrier-funded there is no depreciation hold.

## Cases (hypothetical figures, carrier-funded final draw)

Dwelling depreciation withheld $7,200.00; released $3,000.00; written off as depreciation forfeited $1,100.00.

| Arrangement bills carrier-denied amounts to the customer | Depreciation hold |
|---|---|
| yes | $7,200.00 less $3,000.00, that is $4,200.00 |
| no | $7,200.00 less $3,000.00 less $1,100.00, that is $3,100.00 |

Where the release and the forfeited write-offs together reach the withheld amount, the hold under the second case is zero, never a negative figure.
